scenes.say: How do you track changes in things like customer addresses over time?
There are two main types. Type One just overwrites the old value, so you lose history. Type Two adds a new record for every change, letting you keep all historical data.

rows.b: Insert new row, set valid from date

scenes.say: For example, with Type One, you simply update the address. With Type Two, you insert a new row and set a valid from date.

scenes.label: History
scenes.sub: Use Type 2 if you need to analyze past data.
scenes.say: My advice? Use Type Two when you need to analyze how things looked in the past.

scenes.question: Which SCD type preserves history?
scenes.right: Type 2 creates new records and preserves history
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: only Type Two actually preserves historical data. Type One just overwrites it.
